claims.text: High configurational entropy and severe local lattice distortion jointly govern thermal stability and resistance to atomic diffusion in nearly equiatomic five-transition-metal HEA nanoparticles.
The combined entropy and lattice-distortion effects suppress grain growth and elemental segregation below a critical nanoparticle size threshold.
At sufficiently high surface-to-volume ratio, surface-energy minimization drives rapid Ostwald ripening or phase separation.
Surface-driven evolution can override the bulk sluggish-diffusion effect in five-component HEA nanoparticles.
Non-equilibrium fast cooling or entropy-driven synthesis of nearly equiatomic five-transition-metal nanoparticles produces a single-phase solid solution with statistically distributed elements.
HEA nanoparticles produced by these routes possess high local lattice distortion.
Diffusion coefficients in HEA nanoparticles are size-dependent because of surface-stress effects.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the single-phase solid solution by lowering its Gibbs free energy.
Local lattice distortion impedes atomic migration and thereby causes sluggish diffusion.
Slow diffusion can provide thermal stability and reduce grain-growth rates in HEAs.
A surface-energy contribution scaling inversely with particle radius becomes dominant as particle size decreases.
Decreasing particle size accelerates surface diffusion pathways, causing premature phase separation or grain coarsening relative to bulk material.
Particles larger than a critical radius retain a single phase and exhibit slow grain growth comparable to bulk HEAs.
Particles smaller than the critical radius undergo rapid grain growth, phase segregation, or amorphization.

Traditional alloying concepts treat stability as governed primarily by mixing enthalpy and simple solid-solution rules and may predict equiatomic mixtures to be unstable when configurational entropy is omitted.
Below approximately 10 nm, surface energy dominates over bulk configurational entropy.
A sufficiently negative mixing enthalpy can favor intermetallic formation over a solid solution regardless of configurational entropy.

The cited evidence addresses sluggish diffusion and lattice distortion in bulk HEAs and in 13-, 17-, or 21-component HEA nanoparticles, but does not directly establish the proposed failure mode in nearly equiatomic five-component nanoparticles.
The critical radius at which surface effects override entropy stabilization is unknown.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis initially says entropy and lattice distortion suppress growth and segregation below a critical nanoparticle size threshold, but the predicted outcome and boundary state the opposite: particles below the critical size or radius become unstable because surface effects dominate.
